title: Derived tensor product
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a chosen algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and a finite intermediate extension $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Use the Weil complexes of [def-wf-weil-category] and its coefficient category $D^b_c(X,E)$, namely the rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] of the integral category specified there. Write $\Phi_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, where $\gamma:z\mapsto z^{1/q}$ is the geometric Frobenius automorphism of $k$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. The notation $\Phi_X^*$ means the completed pullback followed by rationalization specified in [def-wf-weil-category]. In this scheme-automorphism case that node identifies completed pullback with coefficient transport, so the explicit inverse-image comparison below uses this same functor.

Here is the derived tensor convention, including the coefficient model implicit in $D(X,E)$. On a small ringed site $(\mathcal C,R)$, choose complexes $C,D$ representing $M,N\in D(R)$, and a quasi-isomorphism $P\to C$ with $P$ K-flat and with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Define
$$
 M\otimes_R^L N=Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R D),
$$
where total tensor is [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and $Q_R$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Use the derived bifunctor obtained by localization [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]; thus this is computation by a K-flat replacement of the first argument, not a requirement of a functorial choice of complex representatives.

For the adic coefficient category above put $A=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi$, and let $A_X=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_X$ be the completed sheaf on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Write $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(A_X)$ for the full subcategory of $D(A_X)$ of objects whose completion map in [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] is an isomorphism. The ambient notation $D(X,E)$ here means $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(A_X)[1/\varpi]$, using raw scalar localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Its bounded constructible objects are the objects selected by [def-wf-weil-category], with its given proper-base-change integral definition. For integral representatives $M,N$ of arbitrary objects in this ambient rational category define the tensor construction by
$$
 M\mathbin{\widehat\otimes}_A^L N
   :=(M\otimes_{A_X}^L N)^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}},
$$
using the completion functor $D(A_X)\to D_{\mathrm{comp}}(A_X)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector], represented by the explicit Koszul mapping-fiber model of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Its rationalization is denoted $K\otimes_E^L L$. On localized morphisms the convention is
$$
 (u/\varpi^r)\otimes(v/\varpi^s)
   =(u\mathbin{\widehat\otimes}v)/\varpi^{r+s}.
$$
In particular the coefficient category here is the adic rationalization, with tensor computed by K-flat tensor followed by completion on integral representatives. The restriction of this construction to an exact bifunctor of Weil complexes is a separate property, not an axiom in this definition.

For Weil complexes $(K,\varphi_K)$ and $(L,\varphi_L)$, define their tensor Frobenius by the typed composite
$$
 \varphi_{K\otimes L}:
 \Phi_X^*(K\otimes_E^L L)
 \xrightarrow{\mu_{\Phi_X;K,L}}
 \Phi_X^*K\otimes_E^L\Phi_X^*L
 \xrightarrow{\varphi_K\otimes_E^L\varphi_L}
 K\otimes_E^L L.
$$
Here are the coefficient identifications and the comparison $\mu$. For $P_n=A/\varpi^n$, let $c_n:\Phi_X^{-1}(P_n)_X\xrightarrow{\sim}(P_n)_X$ be the constant-coefficient isomorphisms of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. They are adjoint to the maps sending each constant section to itself [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Hence they preserve the residues of $\varpi$ and multiplication by those residues; their naturality for ring homomorphisms makes them commute with the quotient maps. The coefficient-ring isomorphism used for module pullback is
$$
 c:\Phi_X^{-1}A_X
 \xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_n\Phi_X^{-1}(P_n)_X
 \xrightarrow{\varprojlim_n c_n}\varprojlim_n(P_n)_X=A_X.
$$
The first arrow uses preservation of limits by the inverse-image equivalence in that node. This $c$ preserves the scalar $\varpi$, as is checked after every projection to $(P_n)_X$.

With this ring map use the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] on integral representatives. More explicitly, write $H$ for the exact module transport induced by $\Phi_X^{-1}$ and $c$, before completion and rationalization. Choose flat-term K-flat representatives $U,V$ for $M,N$. Since the inverse-image equivalence preserves colimits and finite products, it preserves the balanced generators and relations defining sheaf tensor. Thus the canonical balanced map $HU^i\otimes_{A_X}HV^j\to H(U^i\otimes_{A_X}V^j)$ is an isomorphism; on local pure tensors it sends $u\otimes v$ to $u\otimes v$ after the coefficient identification $c$. Its inverse commutes with the two differentials and with direct-sum inclusions, so totalization gives inverse chain maps with the differential $d_U\otimes1+(-1)^i1\otimes d_V$. These represent the cited derived tensor comparison. The cited pullback statement ensures that $HU,HV$ are again flat-term K-flat representatives.

To complete this chain map, write $Q_m=[A_X\xrightarrow{\varpi^m}A_X]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ as in [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Applying $c$ in both degrees gives $HQ_m\cong Q_m$; it respects the transition maps since those are $\varpi$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree $0$. Tensor the preceding degreewise maps with this identification to obtain isomorphisms of actual complexes
$$
 H(\operatorname{Tot}(U\otimes_{A_X}V)\otimes_{A_X}Q_m)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}
 \operatorname{Tot}(HU\otimes_{A_X}HV)\otimes_{A_X}Q_m.
$$
They commute with each strict tower transition because $c(\varpi)=\varpi$; no lifting of an arbitrary derived-category map to strict towers is being assumed. Apply the inverse-image equivalence to the product $B$ and the mapping-fiber complex $F$ in the completion definition: the product comparison is the map whose $m$-th component is the $m$-th inverse-image projection, and it commutes with $1-t$ by the transition identity just checked. On $F^i=B^i\oplus B^{i-1}$ use that comparison on both summands. It commutes with the differential $(x,y)\mapsto(d_Bx,(1-t)x-d_By)$, giving the comparison with completion. Rationalize this composite to obtain $\mu_{\Phi_X;K,L}$ in the displayed direction. The source's shorthand $\varphi_K\otimes\varphi_L$ denotes this composite.

proof.text: For wfRationalTensorPullback_exists, first derive naturality of completion from the reflector Hom bijection and the completion comparison unit square. Combine it with the naturality of proEtaleCanonicalTensorComparison to obtain naturality of the integral tensor comparison. Localize its component isomorphisms with scalar-localization.mapIso. Tensor induction in the two Hom variables reduces naturality to the integral equation, using the pure-tensor formulas for the tensor Hom map, pullback Hom map and composition. Every rational object retains an integral object, so component normalization proves uniqueness by isomorphism and natural-transformation extensionality.

For wfSiteDerivedTensor_first, choose a flat-term K-flat resolution V to D. The existing cochain tensor structures and the homotopy-category acyclicity characterization turn acyclic-tensor K-flatness of P into categorical K-flatness. It follows that tensor by P sends V to D to a quasi-isomorphism. The site-derived-tensor descent comparison computes tensor on P,V; localize the tensor quasi-isomorphism and V to D and compose the resulting isomorphisms.

For wfIsoPullback_complete, apply wfPullbackCompletion_exists to the underlying complete object. Its unit square writes the pulled-back completion unit as the composite of the pullback of the old unit with an isomorphism. The old unit is invertible by completeness, so its functorial image and the composite are invertible.

For wfTensorRepresentative_exists, restrict the homotopy tensor comparison and the site-derived-tensor descent comparison to flat-term K-flat complexes. The siteSheafTensorRightIso identifies the two definitions of termwise flatness. Compose with quotientCompQhIso in the source and target to obtain the representative comparison for wfOrdinaryDerivedTensor. Every homotopy-category object receives a quasi-isomorphism from a flat-term K-flat complex by exists_isKFlatResolutionIndependentCoefficients. Apply resolvingRepresentativesFullyFaithfulWhiskering with the homotopy quotient and DerivedCategory.Qh, then transport along quotientCompQhIso. Its fullness lifts the comparison with any other model, and faithfulness proves uniqueness of the normalized isomorphism.

For wfConstructibleInclusion_exists, the integral inclusion preserves addition and A-scalars definitionally. Define its rational Hom action by LinearMap.baseChange. Tensor induction in both morphisms reduces preservation of composition to the integral functor law and the pure-tensor composition formula. The base-change formula gives the required equality after precomposition with rationalization. Uniqueness follows from scalarLocalization_precomp_injective, which expresses every localized morphism as an integral morphism composed with the inverse of a power of the localized scalar.

For wfConstructiblePullback_obj, apply Functor.congr_obj to the normalization equation of wfConstructibleInclusion_exists. Both sides of the required equality are then scalar-localization objects on complete integral objects with the same underlying derived object. Equality of these full-subcategory objects follows by extensionality, since their underlying objects are definitionally equal under pbcIsoIntegralPullback and wfCompletePullback.

For wfRationalTensorHom_exists, prove sectionwise A-linearity of the ordinary sheaf tensor using its sheafification adjunction and balanced tensor generators. Transport bilinearity through the full essentially surjective homotopy quotient. Flat-term K-flat resolutions give right fractions in the resolving full subcategory; the existing descent comparison and localization universal properties then give bilinearity of the chosen derived tensor. The reflector Hom bijection and completion-unit naturality give A-linearity of completion. Form the resulting bilinear Hom map, extend scalars with the tensor-product base-change equivalence, and curry. The base-change formula gives the required product of scalar numerators; tensor induction in both Hom variables proves uniqueness.

For wfPullbackCompletion_exists, first compare the canonical actual-completed-ring completeness predicate with intrinsic completeness in the constant coefficient presentation. The exact coefficient equivalence transports the explicit Koszul unit, its descent gives independence of representatives, and the normalized Koszul-to-quotient comparison and tower-completeness equivalence allow a change of generating list. This identifies completeness with invertibility of the actual reflective completion unit. For an automorphism, ordinary derived pullback and actual derived direct image are adjoint equivalences. The existing unit-compatible direct-image/completion comparison shows that direct image preserves and reflects completeness, and the adjunction unit then shows that pullback preserves completeness. Transport the reflector Hom bijection across this adjunction; the two unique maps between the pulled-back completion and the completion of the pullback are inverse. The same Hom bijection proves uniqueness of the isomorphism with the prescribed unit square.

For wfCompletePullback_linear, verify compatibility of the completed scalar map with each finite quotient projection. Naturality of the constant inverse-image comparison implies that the completed coefficient map preserves these scalars. Pass to its adjoint direct-image ring map and evaluate the constant-sheaf unit to obtain the equality of the actual sectionwise A-scalars. The module direct-image functor is consequently A-linear, so its left adjoint, the specified module pullback, is A-linear. Exact derived-functor linearity and the faithful full-subcategory inclusion give linearity of wfCompletePullback; additivity is inherited in the same way.

For wfConstructible_complete, take the intrinsic-completeness witness contained in the constructible-complete object. Transport its representative back along the exact completed-coefficient presentation equivalence. The descended Koszul completion unit carries completeness to the resulting representative, and the explicit round-trip comparison identifies its unit with the actual intrinsic unit. The normalized completed Koszul/quotient comparison gives tower completeness. Independence of generators and representatives in towerComplete_iff_intrinsic yields completeness for the stipulated generator list and canonical representative, with no extra hypotheses on the scheme or the list.

proof_origin.note: Closed all four remaining holes: wfRationalTensorHom_exists, wfPullbackCompletion_exists, wfCompletePullback_linear, and wfConstructible_complete. No holes or nodes added. Retained the six existing proof steps and all existing public statements. The final Frobenius isomorphism uses a local generic construction with definitionally identical hom and inv, recorded in coord/changes/wfTensorFrobenius-local-construction.md. Added private proved glue for bilinear localization, scalar preservation and the comparison of completeness predicates; used the existing direct-image/completion comparison for the automorphism completion isomorphism. The existing representative comparison is constructed and proved unique through generic categorical helpers, and integral tensor naturality is taken directly from the whiskered comparison, avoiding expansion of its model. The original six-step route is unchanged.

from a $K$-flat replacement of its first argument. For Weil complexes
$(K,\varphi_K)$, $(L,\varphi_L)$ the tensor Frobenius is
$\varphi_K\otimes\varphi_L$.
